advances: The unrestricted second-moment hypothesis (H2) reduces, with an explicit loss of at most a factor four and a singleton alternative, to full-dimensional complete log-affine tables having quantitative bounds on every proper face and arbitrarily small normalized atoms. This does not establish the required positive lower bound on that restricted class. Combining such a bound with accepted fact 2f0204d9d167faa7 gives the stated quantitative conditional implication for the locked weak Oertel conjecture.
author: research-agent
external_sources: None. The intrinsic lattice construction, partition inequality, completeness of the face and its complement, descent, threshold identities, product-face classification, and atom dilution are proved above. The sole declared accepted predecessor 2f0204d9d167faa7 is used for its exact (H2) normalization and its conditional implication from (H2) to actual mixed-integer depth. No archived research note or unavailable attachment is used as a proof premise.
proof:
The support \(D\) is finite because \(Q\) is compact, and \(P=\operatorname{conv}D\) has exactly the same integer points: the inclusion \(P\subseteq Q\) gives \(P\cap\mathbb Z^N\subseteq D\), and the opposite inclusion is immediate. Replacing \(Q\) by \(P\) therefore does not change the law or any depth. In particular the support hull is a lattice polytope, even when the originally supplied \(Q\) is not a polytope.

We first justify intrinsic lattice coordinates, including depth. Choose \(\mathbf z_0\in D\), let \(V=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}(D-\mathbf z_0)\), let \(r=\dim V\), and put \(L_V=V\cap\mathbb Z^N\). This lattice has a group basis \(\mathbf b_1,\ldots,\mathbf b_r\) which is also a real basis of \(V\). Here is an elementary justification. Any subgroup of \(\mathbb Z^N\) has a real-linearly-independent group basis, by induction on \(N\): if its first-coordinate projection is zero, apply induction in the last \(N-1\) coordinates; otherwise this projection is \(m\mathbb Z\) for its smallest positive element \(m\), choose one group element with first coordinate \(m\), and subtract its integer multiples to reduce every other group element to the kernel of this projection. Apply induction to the kernel. The selected first element and the kernel basis are real-linearly independent because their first coordinates separate them. Applied to \(L_V\), their real span is \(V\), since \(D-\mathbf z_0\subseteq L_V\) already spans \(V\). The number of basis elements is therefore \(r\).

For \(r\ge1\), the affine isomorphism \(T:\mathbb R^r\to\mathbf z_0+V\) given by \(T(\mathbf u)=\mathbf z_0+\sum_{i=1}^r u_i\mathbf b_i\) maps \(\mathbb Z^r\) bijectively onto \((\mathbf z_0+V)\cap\mathbb Z^N=\mathbf z_0+L_V\). It follows that \(T^{-1}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^r=T^{-1}(D)\), and this polytope has dimension \(r\). Writing \(\ell'_i=\boldsymbol\ell\cdot\mathbf b_i\) shows that the transformed weights are proportional to \(e^{\boldsymbol\ell'\cdot\mathbf u}\), since the factor \(e^{\boldsymbol\ell\cdot\mathbf z_0}\) cancels in normalization.

An ambient closed halfspace containing a supported point restricts to either a closed halfspace in \(\mathbf z_0+V\) or its entire affine hull; an empty intersection cannot contain that point. Conversely, every closed halfspace in that affine hull extends to an ambient closed halfspace, by extending its linear functional from \(V\) to \(\mathbb R^N\). The whole affine hull has mass one and cannot lower the infimum below that over the intrinsic halfspaces. The coordinate map \(T\) also carries intrinsic halfspaces bijectively to halfspaces in \(\mathbb R^r\). Thus the probability depths and \(M_2\) are unchanged, and the intrinsic normalized moment is \(\Phi_r=4^{r-N}\Phi_N\le\Phi_N\). If \(r=0\), there is just one supported point; every containing ambient halfspace contains its unit mass, so its depth is one and \(\Phi_0=1\le\Phi_N\). These arguments also apply to every nonempty conditional support used below.

For any finite positive law and any partition of its support into nonempty sets \(A\) and \(B\), let \(m=p(A)\in(0,1)\) and let \(p_A,p_B\) be the conditional probability laws, with depths in their respective affine hulls. For \(\mathbf z\in A\), every containing ambient closed halfspace has mass at least \(m\tau_{p_A}(\mathbf z)\), by restricting it to the affine hull of \(A\). The full-hull and singleton cases are covered by the preceding argument. Taking the infimum and then summing the squared bound over \(A\) gives a contribution at least \(m^3M_2(p_A)\): one factor \(m\) comes from the probability weights and two from the squared depth. The same reasoning on \(B\) proves

\[
M_2(p)\ge m^3M_2(p_A)+(1-m)^3M_2(p_B).
\tag{7}
\]

We next check the constants. For \(k\ge1\), \(\theta_k\) is the unique positive root of \(f_k(x)=(4^k-1)x^2+3x-3\). This follows directly from the quadratic formula. On \([0,\infty)\) the polynomial is strictly increasing, and \(f_k(0)=-3<0<f_k(1)=4^k-1\), so \(0<\theta_k<1\). Substitution at \(k=1\) gives \(\theta_1=(\sqrt5-1)/2>1/2=\theta_0/2\). For \(k\ge1\), use \(f_k(\theta_k)=0\) to obtain

\[
f_{k+1}(\theta_k/2)
=\frac34\theta_k^2-\frac32\theta_k
=\frac34\theta_k(\theta_k-2)<0.
\tag{8}
\]

Monotonicity of \(f_{k+1}\) gives \(\theta_{k+1}>\theta_k/2\). Rationalizing (1) gives \(\theta_k=6/(\sqrt{12\cdot4^k-3}+3)\); multiplying by \(2^k\) proves the stated asymptotic.

Consider now a full-dimensional current table \(p\) in dimension \(r\ge1\), on \(D=P\cap\mathbb Z^r\) with \(P=\operatorname{conv}D\). Let \(F\) be a nonempty proper face of codimension \(k\), with mass \(m=p(F)\). Choose an exposing functional \(\mathbf u\ne\mathbf0\) and a value \(c\) such that \(\mathbf u\cdot\mathbf x\le c\) on \(P\) and \(F=P\cap\{\mathbf u\cdot\mathbf x=c\}\). Put \(A=D\cap F\) and \(B=D\setminus F\). Maximizing the functional in a convex combination of points of \(D\) shows \(F=\operatorname{conv}A\). Hence \(A\) is nonempty and its affine rank is exactly \(r-k\). The set \(B\) is nonempty, since otherwise \(P\subseteq F\), contrary to properness. All weights are positive, so \(0<m<1\).

The face support is complete because \(F\cap\mathbb Z^r=D\cap F=A\). For the complement, set \(c_B=\max_{\mathbf z\in B}\mathbf u\cdot\mathbf z<c\) and let \(P_B=P\cap\{\mathbf u\cdot\mathbf x\le c_B\}\). Then \(P_B\) is compact and convex and \(P_B\cap\mathbb Z^r=B\): every element of \(B\) meets the truncation by the definition of \(c_B\), every element of \(A\) fails it, and every integer point of \(P_B\subseteq P\) belongs to \(D\). In particular \(\operatorname{conv}B\cap\mathbb Z^r=B\) as well, since \(B\subseteq\operatorname{conv}B\subseteq P_B\). Passing either conditional support to its intrinsic coordinates preserves these completeness identities. Conditional normalization only changes the common denominator of the original exponential weights, so both conditional laws remain log-affine.

Let \(r_B\le r\) be the rank of \(B\), and express both conditional laws in their intrinsic coordinates. Applying (7) and multiplying by \(4^r\) gives

\[
\Phi_r(p)\ge
4^k m^3\Phi_{r-k}(p_A)
+4^{r-r_B}(1-m)^3\Phi_{r_B}(p_B).
\tag{9}
\]

This formula includes rank-zero branches, with \(\Phi_0=1\). If \(m\ge\theta_k\), then

\[
4^k m^3+(1-m)^3
=1+m\bigl((4^k-1)m^2+3m-3\bigr)
=1+m f_k(m)\ge1.
\tag{10}
\]

The coefficient \(4^{r-r_B}\) in (9) is at least one. Therefore the sum of the two coefficients in (9) is at least one, and (9) implies \(\min\{\Phi_{r-k}(p_A),\Phi_{r_B}(p_B)\}\le\Phi_r(p)\). Select a conditional law attaining this minimum. It has strictly smaller support cardinality than the current law, and it is again a complete log-affine law in its intrinsic coordinates.

Starting with the intrinsic version of the original table, repeat this operation whenever there is a nonempty proper face of mass at least its corresponding \(\theta_k\). The support cardinality is a positive integer and decreases at every operation, so the procedure terminates after finitely many steps. Every selected intrinsic normalized moment is no larger than the preceding one and hence no larger than the original \(\Phi_N(p)\). If termination occurs at a singleton, its intrinsic normalized moment is one, proving \(\Phi_N(p)\ge1\). Otherwise the terminal table \(q\) has intrinsic dimension \(r\ge1\), is full-dimensional in its intrinsic coordinates, and has no face of mass at least the corresponding \(\theta_k\). In particular it satisfies all the weak inequalities in (2). This proves the descent claim. Choosing faces only when their mass is strictly larger would also suffice, but the stated procedure covers equality in the coefficient estimate explicitly.

It remains to prove the product statements and the quantitative consequence. Let \(q\) be a full-dimensional table in dimension \(r\ge1\) satisfying the face restrictions, with support hull \(P_q\), and let \(L\ge2\) be an integer. Its product law is supported on

\[
\bigl(P_q\times[0,L-1]\bigr)\cap\mathbb Z^{r+1}
=(P_q\cap\mathbb Z^r)\times\{0,\ldots,L-1\},
\qquad
(q\otimes\lambda_L)_{(\mathbf z,j)}=q_{\mathbf z}/L.
\tag{11}
\]

The support hull is the displayed product polytope, which has dimension \(r+1\). Its weights are log-affine, with linear coefficient zero in the last coordinate. For any closed halfspace \(H\subseteq\mathbb R^r\) containing \(\mathbf z\), the cylinder \(H\times\mathbb R\) is a closed halfspace containing \((\mathbf z,j)\), of product mass \(q(H)\). Taking infima gives \(\tau_{q\otimes\lambda_L}(\mathbf z,j)\le\tau_q(\mathbf z)\). Squaring and summing with the product probabilities proves \(M_2(q\otimes\lambda_L)\le M_2(q)\), and hence the first inequality in (3). The atom identity in (3) follows directly from (11).

For completeness, every nonempty face of \(P_q\times[0,L-1]\) is a product \(F\times J\), where \(F\) is a nonempty face of \(P_q\), possibly \(P_q\) itself, and \(J\) is either the whole interval or one of its endpoints. Indeed, an exposing functional has the form \((\mathbf x,t)\mapsto\mathbf u\cdot\mathbf x+vt\). Its maximum on the product is the sum of the maxima on the factors, and equality holds exactly when both coordinates maximize their respective terms. Its maximizing set is therefore precisely the stated product; conversely such factor faces give product faces by choosing their exposing functionals. Codimensions add because dimensions of products add.

If \(J=[0,L-1]\) and the product face is proper, then \(F\) is proper and its mass and codimension are unchanged. Its required bound therefore follows from that of \(q\). If \(J\) is an endpoint, write \(k=\operatorname{codim}F\), allowing \(k=0\) and \(F=P_q\). The factor bound \(q(F)\le\theta_k\) is valid also for \(k=0\), since \(q(P_q)=\theta_0=1\). The product face has codimension \(k+1\), and its mass is

\[
(q\otimes\lambda_L)(F\times J)=q(F)/L
\le\theta_k/2<\theta_{k+1}.
\tag{12}
\]

Thus all face restrictions survive this product, including faces formed from the entire first factor and faces of largest codimension.

Given the fixed \(\varepsilon>0\), choose any integer \(L\ge\max\{2,\lceil2^{r+1}\max q/\varepsilon\rceil\}\). Equation (3) then makes the product satisfy the atom bound in (4). Under the restricted lower-bound premise, it follows that

\[
\kappa\le\Phi_{r+1}(q\otimes\lambda_L)
\le4\Phi_r(q)\le4\Phi_N(p).
\tag{13}
\]

Together with the singleton alternative \(\Phi_N(p)\ge1\), this proves (5) for every original ambient dimension and affine rank.

Hypothesis (H2) in accepted fact 2f0204d9d167faa7 states that there is an absolute \(a>0\) such that \(M_2(p)\ge a^2 4^{-N}\) for every table in the unrestricted class, with no full-dimensionality assumption. An unrestricted (H2) bound immediately restricts to (4) with \(\kappa=a^2\). Conversely, (5) gives exactly (H2) with \(a^2=\min\{1,\kappa/4\}\). This proves the asserted equivalence with the predecessor's normalization.

To prove the sequential failure claim, suppose (H2) fails. Since all normalized moments are nonnegative, for each integer \(j\ge1\) choose an unrestricted table \(p^{(j)}\) in an ambient dimension \(m_j\ge1\) with \(\Phi_{m_j}(p^{(j)})<1/(8j)\). The descent cannot end at a singleton, because this original value is less than one. It produces a full-dimensional table \(q_j\) in some dimension \(r_j\ge1\), with every face bound and \(\Phi_{r_j}(q_j)\le\Phi_{m_j}(p^{(j)})\). Choose the interval length for this table so that the product has normalized maximum atom at most \(1/j\). By (3) and (12), this product, denoted \(p_j\) and of dimension \(N_j=r_j+1\), still has all the face bounds, satisfies \(2^{N_j}\max p_j\le1/j\), and has \(\Phi_{N_j}(p_j)<1/(2j)\). Both required limits follow. This is only a conditional sequence construction from failure of (H2).

Finally, under the restricted positive lower bound, (5) supplies (H2) with the absolute constant \(a=\sqrt{\min\{1,\kappa/4\}}\). Apply the actual-body consequence (2) of accepted fact 2f0204d9d167faa7 with exactly this normalized second-moment hypothesis. It yields one point \(\mathbf y^\star\in S\) whose depth is at least \(a2^{-n}\mathcal H_d(S)/(12\sqrt5)\), and therefore gives (6) for every closed containing ambient halfspace. The point is chosen before that arbitrary halfspace, as required by the locked quantifier order. If \(\mathcal H_d(S)=0\), the conclusion holds at any point of the assumed nonempty \(S\). Taking the displayed smaller \(c_0\) puts the constant in the required interval without changing any hypotheses. This application uses the predecessor's proved conditional transfer only; it does not assume an unproved restricted lower bound as an established fact.
statement:
For an integer \(N\ge1\), let \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^N\) be compact and convex with nonempty \(D=Q\cap\mathbb Z^N\), and let \(\boldsymbol\ell\in\mathbb R^N\). A complete log-affine probability table on \(D\) has weights

\[
\begin{aligned}
p_{\mathbf z}&=\frac{e^{\boldsymbol\ell\cdot\mathbf z}}{\sum_{\mathbf x\in D}e^{\boldsymbol\ell\cdot\mathbf x}},&
\tau_p(\mathbf z)&=\inf_{\substack{H\subseteq\mathbb R^N\text{ a closed halfspace}\\\mathbf z\in H}}\sum_{\mathbf x\in D\cap H}p_{\mathbf x},\\
M_2(p)&=\sum_{\mathbf z\in D}p_{\mathbf z}\tau_p(\mathbf z)^2,&
\Phi_N(p)&=4^NM_2(p).
\end{aligned}
\]

The depth is normalized, exactly as in hypothesis (H2) of accepted fact 2f0204d9d167faa7. Put \(P=\operatorname{conv}D\). A table is called full-dimensional when \(\dim P=N\); face dimensions and codimensions refer to this support hull. Faces of a polytope are its intersections with supporting hyperplanes, with the whole polytope also allowed as a face. The mass \(p(F)\) is \(\sum_{\mathbf z\in D\cap F}p_{\mathbf z}\). An intrinsic table is the same probability law expressed in lattice coordinates in its affine hull. For intrinsic rank zero, its only table is the singleton law, whose depth is defined to be one, agreeing with its depth in every positive-dimensional ambient space. Thus \(M_2=\Phi_0=1\) for a singleton intrinsic table.

Define \(\theta_0=1\) and, for every integer \(k\ge1\),

\[
\theta_k=\frac{\sqrt{12\cdot4^k-3}-3}{2(4^k-1)}.
\tag{1}
\]

In particular \(\theta_1=(\sqrt5-1)/2\), \(\theta_{k+1}>\theta_k/2\) for every \(k\ge0\), and \(2^k\theta_k\to\sqrt3\).

Every complete log-affine table \(p\), of any ambient dimension \(N\ge1\) and any affine rank, admits the following descent. Either \(\Phi_N(p)\ge1\), or there is a full-dimensional complete log-affine table \(q\) in some integer dimension \(r\ge1\) such that

\[
\Phi_r(q)\le\Phi_N(p),\qquad
q(F)\le\theta_{\operatorname{codim}F}
\quad\text{for every nonempty proper face }F\text{ of }\operatorname{conv}(\operatorname{supp}q).
\tag{2}
\]

For every table \(q\) satisfying (2) and every integer \(L\ge2\), its product with the uniform probability law \(\lambda_L\) on \(\{0,\ldots,L-1\}\) is a full-dimensional complete log-affine table in dimension \(r+1\), satisfies the same face restrictions with the corresponding codimensions, and obeys

\[
\Phi_{r+1}(q\otimes\lambda_L)\le4\Phi_r(q),\qquad
2^{r+1}\max(q\otimes\lambda_L)=\frac{2^{r+1}\max q}{L}.
\tag{3}
\]

Consequently, fix any \(\varepsilon>0\). Suppose there is a \(\kappa>0\), independent of dimension and table, such that every full-dimensional complete log-affine table \(p\) in every dimension \(N\ge1\) satisfying

\[
p(F)\le\theta_{\operatorname{codim}F}\quad\text{for every nonempty proper face }F,\qquad
2^N\max_{\mathbf z\in D}p_{\mathbf z}\le\varepsilon
\tag{4}
\]

has \(\Phi_N(p)\ge\kappa\). Then every complete log-affine table, without a rank or atom restriction, satisfies

\[
\Phi_N(p)\ge\min\{1,\kappa/4\}.
\tag{5}
\]

Thus the existence of a positive unrestricted (H2) constant is equivalent to the existence of a positive lower bound on the class (4), for any one fixed \(\varepsilon>0\). If (H2) fails, there is a sequence of full-dimensional complete log-affine tables \(p_j\), in dimensions \(N_j\ge1\), satisfying every face bound in (4), with \(2^{N_j}\max p_j\to0\) and \(\Phi_{N_j}(p_j)\to0\).

Under the restricted lower-bound premise, put \(a=\sqrt{\min\{1,\kappa/4\}}>0\). For every \(n,d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), every convex body \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+d}\), and \(S=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)\ne\varnothing\), accepted fact 2f0204d9d167faa7 then supplies one \(\mathbf y^\star\in S\) such that every closed ambient halfspace \(H\) containing \(\mathbf y^\star\) satisfies

\[
\mathcal H_d(S\cap H)\ge
\frac{\sqrt{\min\{1,\kappa/4\}}}{12\sqrt5}\,2^{-n}\mathcal H_d(S).
\tag{6}
\]

In particular the locked conjecture follows conditionally with \(c_0=\min\{a/(12\sqrt5),1/(2e)\}\in(0,1/e)\). Neither the restricted lower-bound premise nor (H2) is asserted unconditionally.
